Two result columns are computed by an aggregate (transform `aggregated`):
- last_touch_ts: aggregated from evt.activity.kind, lgx.package_event.event_ts and evt.activity.created_at.
- touch_sources: aggregated from evt.activity.kind.
The other 17 result columns have no aggregated value edge. No boundaries or refusals were reported.

`evt.activity.kind` is the only source column for `touch_sources`. It feeds it as an aggregated value, with a pre-aggregation phase (edge c5413e46891d780d17f6a49e, line 23). I found no filter edge from any evt.activity column, so the graph does not show a filter column restricting which activity rows are counted. The only filters in the query are pre-aggregation filters on the whole result, from lgx.shipment_header and lgx.shipment_line columns. Grouping is decided by two influences: evt.activity.entity_id (92c912f5609982d755a7456f) and lgx.package_event.shipment_id (316cb13225db89fce37e1b64). No boundaries or refusals apply.

Four source columns only filter rows (all pre-aggregation, line 23) and never feed or influence any column of the result: lgx.shipment_line.line_status, lgx.shipment_header.updated_at, lgx.shipment_header.is_deleted, lgx.shipment_line.promise_date. The other filter columns (shipped_qty, unit_selling_price, shipment_id, status_code) also supply values to result columns, so they are excluded. No boundaries or refusals in the file.

Four source columns both filter the result (pre-aggregation, line 23) and feed one of its columns by value:
- lgx.shipment_line.unit_selling_price feeds ext.
- lgx.shipment_line.shipped_qty feeds ext and shipped_qty.
- lgx.shipment_header.shipment_id feeds carrier_name and shipment_id.
- lgx.shipment_header.status_code feeds the column named "from".
The other filter columns (line_status, updated_at, is_deleted, promise_date) only filter and feed no column of the result. No boundaries or refusals apply.

Five result columns are NULL-able this way. Each is fed through a LEFT JOIN to a CTE that filters its own rows, so the filter column is a `conditional` value source (not a row filter):
- `primary_email` and `contact_role`: `crm.contact.is_primary` (`WHERE ct.is_primary` in the `nested` CTE, LEFT JOINed as n).
- `Ship To Site` and `site_segment`: `crm.customer_site.country_code` (`country_code = 'US'` in the `site` CTE, LEFT JOINed as st).
- `status_name`: `gold.dim_status.datasource_num_id` (`= 100` in the `status` CTE, LEFT JOINed).

Not counted: `carrier_name` also has `conditional` edges, but they come from a scalar subquery in the select list, not a LEFT-joined CTE. No boundaries or refusals apply to this file.

Two columns of <result:pasted/query11111.sql> take value from evt.activity.kind: last_touch_ts and touch_sources. Both edges are pre-aggregation value edges with transform `aggregated` (statement line 23), so yes, both change through an aggregate. The graph shows no filter or influence edges from this column in that file. The file has no boundaries or refusals.

Two source columns influence `last_touch_ts` as grouping keys (INFLUENCES, pre-aggregation, line 23): `evt.activity.entity_id` and `lgx.package_event.shipment_id`. The aggregated values are different columns: `evt.activity.created_at`, `evt.activity.kind` and `lgx.package_event.event_ts`. No boundaries or refusals apply.

Two columns of <result:pasted/query11111.sql> are affected by lgx.package_event (statement pasted/query11111.sql#<script>:23). last_touch_ts: event_ts is a value source (FEEDS, aggregated) and shipment_id is an influence (grouping key). touch_sources: shipment_id is an influence (grouping key). event_type and location_code have no edges into this result. No boundaries or refusals apply.

The ext > 0 filter relies on lgx.shipment_line.shipped_qty and lgx.shipment_line.unit_selling_price (pre-aggregation FILTERS edges to the result, line 23). The same two columns also supply ext's value: both FEED it with a derived transform (line 23). Other filters on the result (shipment_header.is_deleted, shipment_id, status_code, updated_at; shipment_line.line_status, promise_date) do not feed ext. The graph doesn't tie them to the ext > 0 condition, so they are not cited. No boundaries or refusals.
